title: Hidden-layer backpropagation

pages.title: Continue backward from the output delta
pages.subtitle: Keep the original weights and the Lesson17 forward cache.
blocks: The goal is four hidden deltas and all twelve hidden-layer parameter gradients. The three output gradients were calculated in Lesson18.
Each delta is the derivative of this one example loss with respect to one neuron preactivation. No batch averaging or parameter update happens here.

pages.title: Sum downstream paths, then apply the local slope
pages.subtitle: Handout page 3, sections 5.3-6: every outgoing connection is a dependency.
blocks: The incoming backward derivative is also called the upstream gradient; it comes from downstream neurons in the forward graph. For each next-layer neuron k, multiply its delta by the connecting weight. Add all these path contributions, then multiply by the current neuron sigmoid slope.
A hidden neuron has no direct target label. Do not use hidden activation minus target as its delta. The y-t shortcut was specific to the output sigmoid plus BCE.
Use original connecting weights. Updating the output weights before computing hidden deltas would mix two different parameter states.

pages.title: Why the first hidden neuron needs both paths
pages.subtitle: The diagram isolates its two outgoing connections to hidden layer 2.
blocks: The two next-layer neurons both depend on this first-hidden activation. The chain rule adds the effects through both branches, even when a connecting weight is negative.

pages.title: Checkpoint: every hidden parameter is covered
pages.subtitle: All values are derivatives of the same one-example loss at the same original state.
blocks: The twelve hidden gradients plus three output gradients cover all fifteen trainable parameters. Independent finite-difference checks of all fifteen agree.

pages.title: Your turn: propagate the target-flip delta
pages.subtitle: Use the original input (1,2), original parameters, but target t = 0.
blocks: The forward cache is unchanged, as shown in Lesson18. Recalculate both layer-2 deltas, both layer-1 deltas, and all twelve hidden-parameter gradients.
Write the separate downstream contributions at layer 1 before adding them. Then apply each neuron local sigmoid slope.
Explain why hidden deltas are not hidden y minus target, and why you cannot update an output weight before this calculation.

pages.title: Practice check: what changed and what did not?
pages.subtitle: The known target changed the output delta; all forward values stayed fixed.
blocks: All twelve hidden gradients were recalculated on the preceding pages. Their signs reverse relative to target 1 because the output delta changes sign and all other factors stay fixed.

Here every gradient is multiplied by the same ratio of new to old output delta. That is a check for this fixed-input, fixed-parameter, single-output example; it does not replace the chain-rule working.
Common mistakes: dropping a downstream path, using an incoming instead of outgoing weight in the delta, using a preactivation as a source, or changing weights before all gradients are ready.
